name: Node (Vertex)
definition: An individual, device or category represented as a circle in a graph.
example: In a social network graph each person is a node; in a network diagram each router or computer is a node.

name: Edge (Link)
definition: A line in a graph that joins two nodes and may carry a label or a weight.
example: A friendship between two users, or a cable of 25 m between two buildings.

name: Adjacency Matrix
definition: A grid that records which nodes in a graph are directly linked, using 1 (or a weight) for a link and 0 for none.
example: Row A of a friendship matrix reads 0 1 1 1 0 0, so A is linked to B, C and D.

name: Degree Centrality
definition: A measure of a node's importance based on the number of edges connected to it.
example: A user with 3 friends in a six-person network has degree 3 and normalised degree centrality 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6.

name: Betweenness Centrality
definition: A measure of how often a node lies on the shortest paths between other pairs of nodes, showing which nodes act as bridges.
example: A switch that joins two office floors carries most cross-floor traffic, so it has high betweenness.

name: Connectedness
definition: The property of a graph in which there is a path between every pair of nodes; a graph that is not connected splits into separate components.
example: Cutting the only cable to a building leaves the network disconnected.

name: Weighted Graph
definition: A graph in which each edge has a number, such as a distance, cost or delay.
example: Cable lengths in metres on the links between five sites.

name: Shortest Path
definition: The route between two nodes in a weighted graph with the smallest total weight, which can be found with Dijkstra's algorithm.
example: A to E across cables of 25, 20 and 10 m gives a shortest path of 55 m.

name: Disruptive Technology
definition: A technology that changes how people or organisations do something so much that established products, services or business models are displaced.
example: Streaming services displaced most DVD rental shops.

name: Internet of Things (IoT)
definition: Smart devices and smart objects that send and receive information using the internet and communication infrastructure.
example: A soil moisture sensor that reports readings to a farm's irrigation system.

name: Internet of Me (IoMe)
definition: Technology that connects our minds and bodies with the online world, turning biological and cognitive life into streams of data that can be monitored, shared and shaped.
example: A smartwatch that records heart rate and sleep and shares them with a health app.

name: Edge Computing
definition: A computing framework that distributes processing capabilities and hardware so applications can be closer to their data source.
example: A gateway on a farm that decides when to switch a pump on without waiting for the cloud.

name: SCADA
definition: Supervisory control and data acquisition: a system of sensors, controllers, networks and operator screens used to monitor and control industrial and infrastructure processes.
example: A water utility monitoring reservoir levels and pump stations from a control centre.

name: Interoperability
definition: The ability of devices and systems from different makers to work together and exchange data.
example: A light bulb from one brand and a hub from another both supporting the Matter standard.

name: MQTT
definition: A lightweight publish/subscribe messaging protocol in which devices publish to topics on a broker and others subscribe to those topics.
example: A sensor publishes to farm/paddock3/soil/moisture and an irrigation controller subscribes.

name: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
definition: A cloud service in which the provider supplies virtual servers, storage and networking and the customer manages the operating system and software.
example: Renting a virtual server in a Sydney cloud region to run a legacy program.

name: Platform as a Service (PaaS)
definition: A cloud service in which the provider supplies the operating system, runtime and tools so developers deploy their own code without managing servers.
example: Deploying a web app to a hosted platform such as Azure App Service.

name: Software as a Service (SaaS)
definition: A cloud service in which the provider runs a complete application that users access over the internet, usually by subscription.
example: Microsoft 365 email and documents, or MYOB accounting.

name: Hybrid Cloud
definition: A combination of private (or on-premises) infrastructure and public cloud, connected so data and applications can move between them.
example: A clinic keeps active records on its own server and copies encrypted backups to a public cloud region.

name: Data Sovereignty
definition: The principle that data is subject to the laws of the country where it is stored; NESA also uses the term for the right of Indigenous Peoples to determine the creation, collection, ownership and application of data about them.
example: Choosing a cloud region in Australia so Australian law applies to customer records.

name: Attenuation
definition: The weakening of a signal as it travels through a medium or across distance.
example: An Ethernet cable run beyond about 100 m loses too much signal to work reliably.

name: Latency
definition: The time a signal takes to travel from sender to receiver, usually measured in milliseconds.
example: A geostationary satellite link has noticeably higher latency than a fibre connection.

name: Bandwidth
definition: The maximum amount of data a connection can carry per second, usually measured in megabits per second.
example: A 100 Mbps nbn plan can carry up to 100 megabits each second.

name: Quality of Service (QoS)
definition: Rules that give priority to important or time-sensitive network traffic over less urgent traffic.
example: A router that prioritises video calls over a large file download.

name: Trusted Platform Module (TPM)
definition: A dedicated security chip that stores cryptographic keys in hardware and helps verify that a device started with trusted software.
example: BitLocker uses a TPM to keep a laptop's drive encryption key safe.
